Knyszyn Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Grądy, Poland

Not demolished. Jews are first recorded in Knyszyn in 1605, with significant settlement developing only in the 18th century; by 1921, 1,235 were mostly murdered at Treblinka in November 1942. This cemetery, located within a former pond complex belonging to King Zygmunt August's residence, was likely established at the beginning of the 18th century, with official community permission granted April 14, 1786 and fencing added at that time. Around 1925, the community purchased an adjoining plot to establish a newer cemetery. This site held 74 victims of a November 2, 1942 deportation massacre. Since 2012, the Zygmunt August Regional Association in Knyszyn has cleared vegetation, marked victims' graves, created a tourist trail, and conducted periodic cleaning.
